title: Sparse Attention Adaptation for Long Reasoning
claim: The earlier prefill-oriented sparse gate pools queries; our decoding variant drops query pooling and projects heads to fit autoregressive generation.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, top-down data flow, shared block structure with highlighted differences
description: Two side-by-side block diagrams, (a) SeerAttention and (b) SeerAttention-R, share the same layout. Q, K and V arrows enter at the top. Dotted lines send Q and K into a gray rounded 'Attn Gate' box. In (a) the gate has two Pooling blocks (green), then Linear (cream), RoPE (light blue), MatMul & Softmax (blue) and Sparsify (gray). Block indices feed a white Block Sparse Flash-Attn (Prefill) box, which sits below a RoPE block and outputs Attention Output. In (b) the Q branch has a Linear block labeled 'reduce to kv heads' in place of the Q Pooling block, and the K branch keeps Pooling. The main box becomes Block Sparse Flash Decoding. The pastel color blocks make the swapped Pooling-to-Linear component the first difference the eye finds.
caption: SeerAttention (Sparse Prefill) and SeerAttention-R (Sparse Decode). In SeerAttention-R, no sequence dimension compression/pooling operation is applied in Query (Q). Given that modern architectures predominantly use GQA, a linear layer projects the Q from its original number of heads down to the number of KV heads, enabling shared sparsity selection in a GQA group.
abstract: We introduce SeerAttention-R, a sparse attention framework specifically tailored for the long decoding of reasoning models. Extended from SeerAttention, SeerAttention-R retains the design of learning attention sparsity through a self-distilled gating mechanism, while removing query pooling to accommodate auto-regressive decoding. With a lightweight plug-in gating, SeerAttention-R is flexible and can be easily integrated into existing pretrained model without modifying the original parameters. We demonstrate that SeerAttention-R, trained on just 0.4B tokens, maintains near-lossless reasoning accuracy with 4K token budget in AIME benchmark under large sparse attention block sizes (64/128). Using TileLang, we develop a highly optimized sparse decoding kernel that achieves near-theoretical speedups of up to 9x over FlashAttention-3 on H100 GPU at 90\% sparsity.
